title: Criteria & SLA playbook for on‑prem/VPC networking, upgrades, and air‑gap requests
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Enterprise prospects frequently submit ad hoc requests for VPC/private/on‑prem deployments that vary widely in networking complexity, upgrade windows, and air‑gap requirements. Current intake lacks consistent scoring and SLA guidance, causing showdown delays, unpredictable engineering scoping, and missed sales timelines.

Goal: Ship a compact, reusable playbook and scoring rubric that PMs and Solutions Engineers can apply at intake to: 1) categorize requests by technical effort and risk, 2) set expected SLAs for feasibility and delivery estimates, and 3) identify required preconditions (network diagrams, approved maintenance windows, legal/compliance checklist) before engineering scoping.

Scope: Non-bug enterprise requests only (customer asks to be onboarded to Private/VPC/on‑prem options, includes air‑gapped/offline installs and coordinated upgrade policies). Excludes dedicated capacity capacity-only billing or purely UI/console feature requests.

Success metrics: 1) reduce average time from intake to engineering scoping from current baseline (measured in days) by 40% over next quarter; 2) >80% of intake requests classified with a preliminary SLA within 3 business days; 3) fewer than 10% of scoping efforts blocked by missing artifacts (network topology, firewall rules, maintenance windows).
acceptance_criteria: A documented scoring rubric (network complexity, air‑gap difficulty, upgrade cadence) with triage thresholds: Band A (low effort), Band B (moderate), Band C (high) and sample-case mapping
An SLA table for intake steps: acknowledgement, artifact collection, engineering feasibility review, and estimate delivery
A one‑page intake checklist template for Sales/SEs listing required artifacts and red flags
A rollout plan for training PMs and SEs and an internal Slack workflow with automated reminders
Confluence page linked from intake form and a Google Sheet for tracking SLA metrics
decision: Adopt a three‑axis rubric (network topology complexity, upgrade and patching constraints, and air‑gap/bandwidth risk). Use this rubric to assign Band A/B/C and map to fixed SLA windows: Band A = 3 business days for scoping estimate; Band B = 7 business days; Band C = 15 business days. Band C triggers mandatory pre‑scoping engineering sync and potential paid discovery. Tradeoffs: a stricter SLA reduces sales friction but increases PM/Eng load; we mitigate by training SEs to collect artifacts up front and by automating reminders in the intake form.
comments: 2026-03-10 Sofia Martinez: Drafted initial problem statement and proposed rubric after reviewing 18 inbound requests from Feb–Mar. Observed common missing artifacts: firewall rules, CIDR ranges, and maintenance windows.

2026-03-11 Liam O'Connor: Reviewed rubric. Suggest clarifying 'band C' to include both technical risk and organizational blockers (e.g., legal approvals). Added note to require security contacts for air‑gap installs.

2026-03-12 Priya Desai (Solutions Eng): Feedback from SE pilot — many customers call small on‑prem installs 'air‑gapped' but mean limited internet egress; propose sub‑tags 'true air‑gap' vs 'limited egress'. Update intake checklist accordingly.

2026-03-13 Engineering review (Tariq Ahmed): Engineering flagged that 'upgrade cadence' needs a compatibility matrix; suggested adding expected supported versions and an automated pre‑check script in the proposal. Also suggested gating Band C on available infra maintenance windows.

2026-03-14 Product review: Shared rubric with Sales Ops and Legal. Sales Ops requested that SLA windows be configurable per account tier; Legal asked for a short paragraph on data residency and audit expectations to include in the checklist. Action items captured below.
2026-03-14 Release planning note: Aim to ship the Confluence playbook and intake form update in private-2026.1; tracking sheet and initial training session scheduled during Cycle 2026-W12.
